title: Public PoC Released for Microsoft Exchange Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution
content_md: A publicly available proof-of-concept (PoC) repository is drawing attention to a potential pre-authentication remote code execution chain affecting on-premises Microsoft Exchange Server deployments. The repository references CVE-2026-62911, an Exchange authentication-bypass vulnerability disclosed after Pwn2Own Berlin 2026. However, defenders should treat published exploit material as unverified until it has been independently tested in a controlled, isolated lab environment. Public PoC Released for Microsoft Exchange Microsoft’s advisory and the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI) classify CVE-2026-62911 as an elevation-of-privilege vulnerability involving a capture-replay authentication bypass, not a standalone unauthenticated RCE flaw. ZDI tracks the issue as ZDI-26-538 and attributes it to improper session management in Exchange authorization. While authentication is normally required, the vulnerable mechanism can reportedly be bypassed under specific conditions. When chained with additional bugs, the weakness can contribute to arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM-level privileges. The issue was reportedly demonstrated by DEVCORE researcher Orange Tsai during Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 as part of a three-vulnerability Exchange exploit chain. The demonstration achieved SYSTEM-level code execution and earned a $200,000 reward.
